cross_identity_pipe_auth.limits: same-user server vs. restricted client of the same user (DACL separation, not real virtual-account service SIDs); non-elevated; no SCM / service SID / session 0; client token made by CreateRestrictedToken, not by SCM.

verdict.H1: NOT confirmed by this probe. V1 OpenThreadToken(TOKEN_QUERY, OpenAsSelf=TRUE) succeeded (error 0) in all variants A-D, including write-restricted client with default DACL SY+throwaway only, and (diag) with an explicit DENY GA for the server user. The expected error 5 never occurred; the A-vs-B control therefore did not discriminate.
verdict.V2: OpenAsSelf=FALSE at SecurityIdentification: success (error 0) in all variants, level=1 (identification), CheckTokenMembership works.
verdict.V3: GetNamedPipeClientProcessId ok, pid == CreateProcess child pid in all variants.
verdict.pipe_DACL: CreateFile admitted the restricted client in all variants (error 0).
verdict.real_code: tools.vst.windows_named_pipe._verify_client_sid on the same handle returned without exception in all variants.
verdict.instrument_check: readback of TokenDefaultDacl ACE counts: original 3, deny+SY+thr 3, SY+thr 2 (setting is stored on the token). Child event-DACL readback returned empty string (instrument limitation, not interpreted).
verdict.limits: Server and client share one user/logon session and the server is an unrestricted non-elevated token; the real server is a virtual account with sidtype restricted (write-restricted token with its own restricting SIDs), different service SID, session 0, possibly different integrity/logon session. DACL-by-default-DACL hypothesis is not the cause on this OS build for same-user pairs; different-user or restricted-server effects remain untested.
